topic: Translating a questionnaire changes more than its words
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: Translating a questionnaire changes more than its words
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立阅读答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
passage:
A. A fictional city research team wanted to compare use of public gardens among residents answering in two languages. It translated an existing questionnaire and assumed that equal wording would create equal questions. A bilingual adviser pointed out that a literal translation might preserve words while changing what respondents understood them to mean.

B. One item asked how often people visited a local park. In one translated version, the chosen term suggested a large formal garden. Residents using small open spaces might answer never even though the original question intended to include those spaces. This was not necessarily an error by the respondent. The category itself had shifted during translation.

C. The team invited speakers of both languages to explain how they interpreted each question. These cognitive interviews were not designed to estimate visiting frequency. Their purpose was to reveal problems in understanding before a larger survey. The team discovered that a question about the previous month was also ambiguous: some people thought of the last calendar month, while others counted back thirty days from the interview.

D. Revisions included a shared definition of eligible green spaces and exact start and end dates for the recall period. The adviser cautioned that clearer wording would not make the two groups identical. Age, working hours and residential location could still affect visiting patterns. A difference between language groups should not automatically be attributed to language itself.

E. The final questionnaire retained a version history recording why each item changed. Results from the early pilot were not merged with the revised main survey because the questions were no longer equivalent. The report also stated which language each participant chose, without treating that choice as a complete description of identity. Careful translation improved the measurement, but responsible interpretation still required attention to the people, contexts and categories behind the answers.

questions.prompt: What assumption did the team initially make?
options: Literal wording would produce equivalent questions.
Different languages necessarily prevent all comparison.
No existing questionnaire could be translated.
Every respondent used the same type of garden.
answers: Literal wording would produce equivalent questions.

questions.prompt: What did the translated park term suggest?
options: Every small open space in the neighbourhood.
Only indoor planting in private homes.
A journey to any distant rural area.
A large formal garden.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“suggested a large formal garden.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。

questions.prompt: What was the purpose of the small interpretive interviews?
options: Proving the translation had no weaknesses.
Ranking all public gardens by attendance.
Finding problems in how questions were understood.
Estimating the whole population’s visiting frequency.
answers: Finding problems in how questions were understood.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“reveal problems in understanding before a larger survey.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。

questions.explanation: 依据原文“These cognitive interviews”。答案按原文填写，保留限定范围。

questions.prompt: What two interpretations of time were found?
options: A calendar month and the preceding thirty days.
The current week and the next calendar year.
Every visit ever made and the next planned visit.
Only mornings and only evenings.
answers: A calendar month and the preceding thirty days.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“the last calendar month, while others counted back thirty days”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。

questions.explanation: 依据原文“the recall period.”。答案按原文填写，保留限定范围。

questions.prompt: Why might a later group difference not be caused by language?
options: The revised questions eliminated all social differences.
Choosing a language defines a person’s complete identity.
Other characteristics could differ between the groups.
Every participant had identical working hours.
answers: Other characteristics could differ between the groups.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“Age, working hours and residential location could still affect visiting patterns.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。
questions.evidence: Age, working hours and residential location could still affect visiting patterns.

questions.prompt: Why were early pilot results kept separate?
options: The team had measured only future visits.
The revised questions were no longer equivalent.
No version history had survived.
All pilot respondents had refused permission.
answers: The revised questions were no longer equivalent.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“the questions were no longer equivalent.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。
questions.evidence: the questions were no longer equivalent.
